limitations_and_boundaries: The exact number of cells needed for future screens will depend on the strength of the investigated biological signal.
Downsampling analysis indicated that 870 cells (15% of dataset) yielded similar results, but scalability may vary by biological context.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

research_questions.statement: Can pooled CRISPR screening be combined with single-cell RNA sequencing to enable transcriptome-wide readouts of genetic perturbations?

provenance.text_excerpt: We found that 870 single cells (15% of the data set) yielded results similar to those of the entire screen.

claims.statement: CROP-seq is scalable: analysis of 870 cells (15% of data) produced TCR signatures concordant with the full dataset.

provenance.text_excerpt: We showed that gene signatures can be derived directly from single-cell data using the transcriptomes of cells with nontargeting gRNAs, which makes the assay self-calibrating and independent of any prior knowledge about relevant marker genes.

claims.statement: CROP-seq can derive gene signatures directly from single-cell data using nontargeting gRNA controls, making the assay self-calibrating.

provenance.text_excerpt: Depletion of the kinases LCK and ZAP70 and the adaptor protein LAT had a strong negative effect on the TCR activation signature ... targeting known negative regulators of TCR signaling (such as PTPN6, PTPN11, and EGR3) slightly increased the TCR activation signature.

claims.statement: CROP-seq can identify known positive and negative regulators of TCR signaling, including LCK, ZAP70, LAT as activators and PTPN6, PTPN11, EGR3 as repressors.

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: Our method for CRISPR droplet sequencing (CROP-seq) enables pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell transcriptome resolution

provenance.text_excerpt: CROP-seq thereby enables pooled screens with single-cell transcriptome readout

claims.statement: CROP-seq enables pooled CRISPR screening with single-cell transcriptome readout by detecting gRNAs directly from polyadenylated mRNA transcripts.

provenance.text_excerpt: Genome editing was highly efficient for both constructs, averaging at 95.5% (LentiGuide-Puro) and 90.5% (CROPseq-Guide-Puro)

claims.statement: CROP-seq achieves high genome editing efficiency (average 90.5%) comparable to the standard LentiGuide-Puro construct.

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: High correlations were observed between bulk RNA-seq and CROP-seq data, both for inferred TCR signature intensities and for global expression profiles (Fig. 2f and Supplementary Fig. 8c,d).

provenance.text_excerpt: Flow cytometry for surface proteins ... further validated the CROP-seq results (Fig. 2g and Supplementary Fig. 9).

claims.statement: CROP-seq results for TCR signaling are concordant with bulk RNA-seq and flow cytometry validation.

datasets.description: 5,798 high-quality single-cell transcriptome profiles with unique gRNA assignments from Jurkat cells; 1,320 control cells with nontargeting gRNAs; median of 80 cells per targeted gene
datasets.name: CROP-seq single-cell RNA-seq data from Jurkat TCR screen

datasets.description: 87 RNA-seq libraries from Jurkat cells with single gene knockouts and controls
datasets.name: Arrayed validation bulk RNA-seq data

evidence_spans.content: CROP-seq reads the gRNA directly, which simplifies single-cell CRISPR screening with large gRNA libraries and is fully compatible with standard cloning protocols for pooled CRISPR screens.

provenance.text_excerpt: CROP-seq has the key advantage that it reads the gRNA directly, which dramatically simplifies single-cell CRISPR screening with large gRNA libraries and makes CROP-seq fully compatible with standard cloning protocols for pooled CRISPR screens.

experiments_or_tasks: Arrayed validation: bulk RNA-seq (87 libraries) and flow cytometry (96 profiles) for 20 targeted genes with two gRNAs each and eight nontargeting controls
CROP-seq lentiviral construct design: insertion of hU6-gRNA cassette into 3' LTR of LentiGuide-Puro to make gRNA detectable by poly-A-based RNA-seq
Detection of gRNAs from single-cell transcriptomes: Drop-seq on a 1:1:1 mixture of HEK293T knockout cell lines (DNMT3B, MBD1, TET2)
Genome editing efficiency assessment: T7 endonuclease assay and next-generation sequencing of PCR amplicons in K562, Jurkat, and HEK293T cells
Proof-of-concept screen: CROP-seq analysis of TCR signaling in Jurkat cells using a library of 87 gRNAs targeting TCR-related genes, 20 nontargeting controls, and 9 essential gene controls
Validation of lentiviral function: comparison of viral titers between LentiGuide-Puro and CROPseq-Guide-Puro for three gRNAs and a filler construct

methods.name: CROP-seq lentiviral construct assembly
methods.protocol_description: CROPseq-Guide-Puro plasmid assembled from four PCR products using ligase cycling reaction; contains hU6-gRNA cassette inserted into the 3' LTR of LentiGuide-Puro

methods.name: Lentivirus production and titration
methods.protocol_description: HEK293T cells seeded at 50,000 cells/well in 24-well plates, transduced with lentivirus in 1:5 dilution series; selection with puromycin or blasticidin; resistant colonies stained with crystal violet after 10-14 days; titer calculated as (colonies × dilution factor) × 20

methods.name: Lentiviral transduction for suspension cells
methods.protocol_description: Jurkat cells at 5 million cells/well in six-well plates with 8 µg/ml polybrene; virus added; plate centrifuged at 37°C and 1,200 RCF for 45 min; selection with puromycin started at 48 h; cells grown for 10 days under selection

methods.name: Anti-CD3/CD28 stimulation
methods.protocol_description: Jurkat cells serum-starved for 3 h, then stimulated with 1 µg/ml anti-CD3 and 1 µg/ml anti-CD28 antibodies for 4 h; naive controls subjected to continued starvation

methods.name: Drop-seq single-cell RNA-seq
methods.protocol_description: Cells and barcoded beads coencapsulated in microfluidic droplets; droplets broken with perfluoroctanol; beads collected by syringe filtration; reverse transcription and exonuclease I treatment; PCR for 4 + 10 cycles; Nextera XT library preparation; sequenced on Illumina HiSeq 3000/4000 or NextSeq 500

methods.name: CROP-seq data preprocessing
methods.protocol_description: Drop-seq Tools v1.12 used: cell barcode (bases 1-12) and UMI (bases 13-20) from Read1 tagged to transcriptome Read2; trimmed reads aligned with STAR v2.4.0 to human reference (GRCh38) plus artificial chromosomes representing CROPseq-Guide-Puro construct; cell barcode correction allowing up to 4 base mismatches; UMI deduplication; digital gene expression matrix built for cells with ≥500 genes; gRNA assignment: most abundant gRNA per cell (dominant gRNA must be >3× sum of others for unique assignment)

methods.name: T7 endonuclease assay
methods.protocol_description: PCR primers designed so gRNA target is off-center; 200 ng purified PCR product denatured and reannealed; digested with 1 µl T7 endonuclease I at 37°C for 15 min; analyzed on Agilent High Sensitivity DNA chip; editing efficiency = average(digested1, digested2) / sum(average(digested1, digested2), undigested)

methods.name: Indel analysis by next-generation sequencing
methods.protocol_description: Amplicons <500 bp with gRNA target at center; PCR purified; Nextera XT library preparation; sequenced on Illumina MiSeq 150-cycle v3 flow cell; reads extracted using anchor sequences; indel size calculated as deviation from expected 100 bp fragment

study_units.name: Development and validation of CROP-seq

provenance.text_excerpt: We produced virus from LentiGuide-Puro and CROPseq-Guide-Puro containing one of three validated gRNAs (targeting DNMT3B, MBD1, or TET2) or a longer filler construct that was expected to interfere with viral activity, and we observed comparable functional titers for all tested gRNA sequences (Fig. 1f).

results.value_raw_text: Comparable functional titers for all tested gRNA sequences (TET2, DNMT3B, MBD1) between LentiGuide-Puro and CROPseq-Guide-Puro; filler construct resulted in 98-fold reduction in viral titer

provenance.text_excerpt: We found that 870 single cells (15% of the data set) yielded results similar to those of the entire screen.

results.value_raw_text: 870 single cells (15% of dataset) yielded results similar to entire screen for TCR signature intensities

provenance.text_excerpt: For example, 38.7% of cells with at least 500 and 78.9% of cells with at least 4,000 detected genes were uniquely assigned. Few cells matched more than one gRNA (e.g., 2.7% for a threshold of 500 detected genes), although this rate increased with the detected number of genes per cell (e.g., 9.8% for a threshold of 4,000).

results.value_raw_text: 38.7% of cells with ≥500 detected genes uniquely assigned; 78.9% of cells with ≥4,000 detected genes uniquely assigned; 2.7% of cells with ≥500 genes matched multiple gRNAs

provenance.text_excerpt: When we applied Drop-seq on a 1:1:1 mixture of the three cell lines, the resulting single-cell transcriptomes provided high sequencing coverage for the gRNAs, and we were able to assign single cells to gRNAs at the expected ratios (Fig. 1h).

results.value_raw_text: In a 1:1:1 mixture of three knockout cell lines (DNMT3B, MBD1, TET2), single-cell transcriptomes provided high sequencing coverage for gRNAs and cells assigned at expected ratios

provenance.text_excerpt: Genome editing was highly efficient for both constructs, averaging at 95.5% (LentiGuide-Puro) and 90.5% (CROPseq-Guide-Puro), with the expected two thirds (66.2% and 62.4%) of molecules carrying out-of-frame insertions and deletions.

results.value_raw_text: Average editing efficiency 95.5% for LentiGuide-Puro and 90.5% for CROPseq-Guide-Puro, with 66.2% and 62.4% out-of-frame indels respectively
